title: Prepositions of place
tagline: Where things are, chez, cities, countries and transport.
goal: Say where things and people are, use chez, choose à, en, au or aux with cities and countries, and say how you travel.

head: French
English
Example
rows: *La poste est {entre} la banque et le café.*

blocks.title: One word each
blocks.text: «in front **of**» is just *devant*: no *de* after these six. *devant le cinéma*, never «devant de le cinéma».
*Sur* and *sous* are easy to mix up. Think of *sous-marin* (submarine) and *sous-sol* (basement): what's underneath is *sous*.

head: French
English
rows: to the left of · to the right of

blocks.text: That *de* merges with the article, like the *à* in [[9]]:
de + le = du · de + les = des · de la and de l' don't change

items.fr: La gare est près {de la} poste.
items.tr: The station is near the post office.

items.fr: Le bus s'arrête à côté {des} magasins.
items.tr: The bus stops next to the shops.

blocks.text: English uses «in» for being there and «to» for going. French uses **the same word** for both, but it depends on the place:

head: Place
Preposition
Example
rows: Masculine country starting with a vowel

blocks.text: *Je suis en France* (I'm in France) and *Je vais en France* (I'm going to France): same preposition.

blocks.title: Exceptions ending in -e
blocks.text: A few countries end in -e but are masculine: *le Mexique, le Cambodge, le Mozambique*. So: *{au} Mexique*.
**To say where you come from**, *de* merges the same way: *Je viens {de} France, {du} Canada, {des} États-Unis, {de} Londres*.
*Chez* means «at / to someone's place», like the English «at the doctor's». It always goes with a **person**, never with a place.

items.tr: I have an appointment at the dentist's.

blocks.title: À or chez?
blocks.text: *à la boulangerie* (the place) = *chez le boulanger* (the person): both «at the baker's».

head: You sit inside: en
You sit on top: à
rows: *{en} voiture, {en} bus, {en} train* (by car, bus, train)
*{à} pied, {à} vélo, {à} moto* (on foot, by bike)

exercises.title: Where is it?
exercises.instructions: Choose the preposition that matches the hint.

items.prompt: La pharmacie est ___ la banque et la poste.
Je t'attends ___ le cinéma. (in front of)

exercises.title: Du, de la, de l', des
exercises.instructions: Write du, de la, de l' or des.

items.prompt: La gare est à côté ___ hôtel.
Il y a un banc au milieu ___ jardin.
Le bus s'arrête en face ___ magasins.

exercises.title: À, en, au or aux
exercises.instructions: Choose the preposition for the city or country.

items.explain: *le Mexique* is masculine even though it ends in -e.
*l'Iran* is masculine but starts with a vowel: *en*.

items.prompt: Ce soir, on dîne ___ mes parents.
The cat is under the table.
items.answer: Le chat est sous la table.

items.prompt: The bank is opposite the hotel.
items.answer: La banque est en face de l'hôtel.

items.prompt: I'm going to Italy by train.
items.answer: Je vais en Italie en train.

checklist: I say where something is with *sur, sous, dans, devant, derrière, entre*.
I use *à côté de, en face de, près de* with *du* and *des*.
I choose *à, en, au, aux* with cities and countries.
I use *chez* with people and say how I travel (*en train, à pied*).

challenge.title: Your neighbourhood
challenge.text: Describe in five sentences where your home is and what's around it: *J'habite à Manchester, près du parc. En face de chez moi, il y a une boulangerie.* End with a country you'd like to visit and how you'd go: *Je voudrais aller au Japon en avion.*
